The Thai economy would contract more than previously assessed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
However, economic activities exhibited signs of improvement following the relaxation of the containment measures.
Headline inflation was projected to be more negative in 2020 than expected but would rise toward the target in 2021.
Economic and inflation forecasts in the period ahead would be subject to high uncertainties and downside risks.
The COVID-19 pandemic was more severe than expected.
Governments in many countries, including Thailand, implemented containment measures which severely affected tourism and merchandise exports.
Domestic demand, both private consumption and private investment, would contract more than the previous assessment.
Employment and incomes were projected to decline.

Additionally announced fiscal, financial, and credit measures helped alleviate adverse impacts and would support economic recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic subsided, facilitate the rise of inflation toward the target, and reduce financial stability risks.
